 Shri Bal Krishna Agrawal, learned counsel for the resp
 Order

This appeal by the appellant/claimant u/S. 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is arising out of the award dated 07.09.2012 passed by MACT, Datia (in short "Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.135/2011 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.

Appellants is further aggrieved by the finding of the Tribunal by which Tribunal totally exonerated the Insurance Company from liability.
2. Date of accident and negligence is not in dispute, however, findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard in not in question.
3.

As per the finding of the Tribunal regarding injury received by the claimant/appellant, the Tribunal awarded Rs. 21,500/- in favour of the claimant with interest @ 7% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization, however, the Tribunal totally exonerated Insurance Company.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16783 2 MA-1320-2012 4.
The appellant filed this appeal on the ground that Tribunal has committed error in exonerating Insurance Company from liability.

He further submitted that Insurance Company did not examine Sukhsingh Pal vs Ramprakash on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144656850/
1 any witness with regard to breach of policy.

sentences.text: Appellant was third party, so Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation and thereafter it may be recovered from the owner/driver of the alleged vehicle.
He further submitted that Tribunal has awarded meager amount of compensation and seeking further enhancement.

5. On the other hand, learned Counsel for the Insurance Company submitted that Tribunal has rightly exonerated insurance company because driver and owner is one and the same person and he had no valid and effective license.
So Tribunal has rightly passed the award and exonerated him.

He relied upon the cases of Malla Prakasarao vs Malla Janaki And Ors reported in (2004) 3 SCC 343 a n d Dhirendra Singh Senghar Vs. Gopi Singh Kalicharan & Another reported in 2008 ACJ 2277 wherein it was held that insurance company cannot be held liable for paying compensation amount if driver and owner is one and the same person.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. On the other hand, learned counsel of the owner and driver submitted that the Tribunal has committed error while exonerating insurance company.

7. After hearing counsel of both the parties and perusal of the record it is undisputed that Respondent No. 1 is owner and driver of the offending vehicle and owner/driver has no valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
So, considering the aforesaid rulings, in considered opinion of this Court, Tribunal has not committed any error in exonerating Insurance Company from its liability.
So finding of the Tribunal in this regard is correct in the eyes of law.
So appellant's appeal on this ground has no substance.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16783 3 MA-1320-2012 8.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that Claims Tribunal has committed grave error in awarding the amount of compensation.

He further submitted that Claims Tribunal has awarded the compensation in lower side, hence it is prayed that compensation amount be enhanced and just and reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded.
9. Learned counsel of the Insurance Company and respondent No. 1-owner and Driver supported the impugned award in this regard.

10. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the record as well as looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, more particularly the age of the injured/claimant and the injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident, it would be appropriate to enhance to lump sum amount of Rs. 25,000/-
only, which has to payed by respondent No.1.
11.
Accordingly, present appeal is allowed in part to the extent indicated herein above.
The amount of compensation is enhanced to lump sum amount of Rs.25,000/- in the present appeal.
The appellant is entitled to receive Rs.25,000/- in addition to the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

The enhanced amount shall carry interest as awarded by the Claims Tribunal from the Sukhsingh Pal vs Ramprakash on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144656850/
2 date of the filing of the claim petition till its realization.
All other findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

12. The present appeal stands disposed of.
